title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure the downstream effect of a deterministic network‑configuration validator plus an allowed single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter label openai_responses) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on N = 200 paired intents (completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared initial candidate passed validator checks so no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. We provide artifact‑grounded methodological detail, representative validator diagnostics, reproducibility mappings, and a focused discussion clarifying the causal limits of the executed estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics and preregistered follow‑on designs needed to measure repair efficacy under independent sampling or adversarial conditions.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for intent→configuration workflows in network operations (NetOps). Translating high‑level intent to device configuration sequences is operationally sensitive: syntactic errors, invalid command ordering, or hallucinated fields can cause redundancy loss, service disruption, or policy violations when deployed. A common architectural mitigation is generate–validate–repair (GVR): generate candidate configuration(s), deterministically validate candidates against topology and policy constraints, and apply automated repair when violations occur. Prior literature documents verifier‑guided improvement in related domains (infrastructure‑as‑code, program repair) and motivates similar pipelines for NetOps, but transferability to device‑level executable safety and the causal role of validators/repair under different sampling semantics remain open questions.

This paper reports a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that intentionally evaluates a narrowly specified estimand: the effect of a deterministic validator and one permitted automated repair on the identical sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Under these semantics, generation sampling variability between conditions is removed by design and any paired difference can only arise from deterministic downstream validation/repair acting on the same candidate. We present artifact‑grounded execution accounting, validator traces from representative tasks, exact paired inference, and a discussion that (a) explains why no repairs were invoked in this run and (b) enumerates preregistered follow‑on estimands required to evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling or adversarial uplift.
sections.related_work:
Hallucination and unreliable factuality in LLM outputs are well documented and motivate grounding and verification strategies for operational tasks [1]. Retrieval‑augmented and evidence‑grounded pipelines reduce hallucination in operations‑style QA, but these works typically evaluate textual fidelity rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulation [2]. Generate→verify→repair architectures have produced measurable improvements for infrastructure‑as‑code and program generation (e.g., verifier‑guided fine‑tuning and iterative repair frameworks) and directly inspired the present GVR design; however, those demonstrations do not present standardized execution‑level device emulation results for NetOps in the supplied literature [3].

NetOps LLM evaluations have assessed intent translation and capability but lack a standardized execution‑level safety benchmark that maps candidate configurations to executable effects in a simulated or emulated network testbed—a gap our execution artifacts and task manifest were designed to begin closing by providing deterministic validator traces and packet‑level emulation plans as follow‑on work [4]. Our study complements prior work by precisely operationalizing a shared_initial_candidate estimand so readers and future experiments can unambiguously separate downstream validator/repair causal effects from sampling or prompting interventions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the complete experimental plan (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01; preregistration SHA‑256: f0c8330d3d74cb95461d3f0291ba1b607c427ad37b5edc3750cad593bd4aae76) before any model calls. The primary estimand is the paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline conditions under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The confirmatory design fixed task_count = 200 paired intents (planned_episode_count = 400) and allowed at most one automated repair per guarded episode; generation semantics were explicitly shared_initial_candidate so each pair reused the same sampled initial generation. The preregistered primary test is the exact two‑sided McNemar test (alpha = 0.05) and we planned a paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) to produce a percentile 95% confidence interval for the paired difference.

Task bank and contamination checks. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed manifest of 200 synthetic "intent_configuration_repair_v1" tasks; each entry records initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotations (e.g., "safe_access_service_transfer", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and a generation_seed for deterministic replay. We executed the preregistered contamination checks (SHA‑256 exact‑match and high‑similarity n‑gram Jaccard) prior to any model calls. No exact‑match exclusions were flagged and the confirmatory sample remained intact; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty in the archived bundle.

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent which was deterministically reused in both baseline and guarded episodes (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The declared generator recorded in execution/model_configuration.json is "gpt‑5‑mini" (adapter: openai_responses); the execution manifest reports model_calls_used = 200 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, consistent with a single shared generation per pair. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); we explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Deterministic validator and permitted repair. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation". The validator produces structured traces (validation_before, validation_after), normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and a boolean validator.valid flag that maps to the binary executable label used in analysis. For guarded episodes a single automated repair attempt was permitted (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 in the preregistration). Repair provider traces, when produced, are archived under execution/scoring/*.json; the analysis pipeline maps validator.valid to success/failure without human adjudication.

Analysis plan and missingness. The primary confirmatory analysis is a paired binary test (exact two‑sided McNemar) on the 2×2 contingency table with the preregistered missingness policy 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs). Sensitivity analysis 'failure‑as‑zero' treats missing/failed episodes as unsafe. Bootstrap parameters (seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) and contingency tallies are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv. All code and result schemas are archived under execution/* and analysis/* in the artifact bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and a completed_pair_count = 200. The analysis missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and records cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Primary outcomes and inferential statistics. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) are baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0 for each condition). The paired contingency table (guarded vs baseline) observed n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. These analytic artifacts are archived under analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv; bootstrap parameters and results are in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Repair activity and validator diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0; no guarded episode required or invoked a repair because no shared initial candidate triggered a validator violation. Representative per‑episode JSON artifacts (for example: execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate content, identical parsed_command_count and required_command_count, and validator.valid = true for both baseline and guarded episodes. Example shared_initial_candidate excerpt (task-000004): "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"; parsed_command_count = 4; required_command_count = 4; validator.valid = true. Representative artifacts for additional hard tasks (task-000005, task-000006, task-000007, task-000008) are archived and summarized in the artifact bundle and Table 2.

Contamination and provider audit. Preexecution contamination checks flagged no exact‑match leaks; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with one shared generation per pair. All deterministic consistency checks passed; reconciliation artifact paths and representative artifact hashes are available in the archived bundle.
sections.discussion:
Causal scope and interpretation. The executed estimand intentionally isolates downstream validator/repair effects on fixed sampled candidates. Because all shared initial candidates were validator‑valid, the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to repair and therefore could not change outcomes. The degenerate contingency (zero discordant pairs) therefore correctly reflects the executed estimand and supplies no evidence about repair efficacy under independent per‑condition sampling or under task distributions with higher validator‑detectable failure rates.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: by design the shared_initial_candidate semantics eliminate sampling differences between conditions; this supports internal attribution for downstream repair effects but prevents evaluation of sampling‑level interventions such as constrained prompting or temperature control. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes a formal mapping from intent constraints to checks (syntax, required sequence, protected interfaces) and returns structured traces; however, it remains an abstraction that does not execute vendor CLI on physical devices nor run packet‑level emulation during scoring. External validity: the run used a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via adapter openai_responses), synthetic task bank, and one validator implementation — therefore generalization beyond these artifacts is unsupported by the archived evidence. Conclusion validity: the absence of discordant outcomes yields no inferential information about repair benefits under broader sampling regimes; the confirmatory test correctly reports p = 1.0 and CI = [0.0,0.0], which reflect the executed data rather than measurement error.

Operational implications and preregistered follow‑on estimands. The artifacts and preregistration include explicit, artifact‑grounded follow‑on designs to measure repair efficacy under operationally relevant conditions: (A) remove shared_initial_candidate and sample independently per condition so baseline and guarded arms receive separate first‑pass candidates—this permits repair to act on validator‑detectable faults but requires a revised paired analysis plan; (B) select only tasks annotated as "extreme" or inject adversarial perturbations to raise expected validator failure rates and thereby exercise the repair path; (C) set explicit, non‑null temperature values and preregister temperature sweeps to study diversity vs validator failure tradeoffs; (D) increase validator fidelity by integrating vendor CLI semantics or packet‑level emulation so repairs are judged against dynamic runtime behavior; (E) run multi‑model/provider sampling to assess generality across generator families. Each follow‑on design is preregisterable using the archived task bank, provider audit traces, and validator interfaces in the artifact bundle.

Why artifact grounding matters. The per‑episode JSON artifacts (execution/scoring/) provide explicit validation_before/after subtables with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and repair_applied flags. These artifacts make transparent why repairs did not execute in this run and allow independent reanalysis of the executed estimand without ambiguity about sampling semantics, retries, or cache reuse. The execution/model_configuration.json explicitly records declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini" and temperature = null; again, null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. The master prompt immutable reference is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt) and reported in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment measuring the downstream effect of a deterministic validator plus an allowed single automated repair on the same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). With gpt‑5‑mini declared as the generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the scorer, all shared initial candidates passed validation and no repairs were attempted or applied; guarded and baseline outcomes were identical for the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Importantly, because the design reused the same sampled candidate across conditions, this result does not assess whether a guarded pipeline reduces generator error rates when sampling independently per condition; independent per‑condition sampling constitutes a distinct preregistered estimand and analysis plan and therefore was not evaluated here. Archived artifacts and reconciliation files enable exact reproduction of the executed estimand and provide a concrete, artifact‑grounded baseline for preregistered extensions that measure repair efficacy under broader sampling, adversarial uplift, and higher‑fidelity validation.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) prior to the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, experiment selection, preregistration (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01; preregistration SHA‑256: f0c8330d3d74cb95461d3f0291ba1b607c427ad37b5edc3750cad593bd4aae76), code generation, execution, deterministic validation, automated analysis, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model used in execution: gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter 'openai_responses' (execution used model_calls_used = 200; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Generation semantics executed: shared_initial_candidate — exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded conditions (no independent per‑condition first‑pass sampling). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored candidates using 'full_intent_constraint_validation' and a single automated repair iteration was permitted in guarded episodes; in this run the validator flagged no violations and no repairs were applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Execution accounting: completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired intents) completed without preregistration deviations; execution manifest and analysis artifacts are archived under execution/* and analysis/*. Master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred but pre‑lock artifacts were not used as empirical evidence in this final run. After the autonomy lock no human manually rewrote technical results, manuscript text, figures, or references.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
